title: Contrastive deep learning finds cell-cycle genes predicting mouse liver regeneration
summary: Six mouse hepatectomy models (young male and female, aged, fibrotic, steatotic, tacrolimus) were profiled, and a contrastive deep-learning framework with triplet loss predicted regenerative outcome with 87.9% accuracy. SHAP highlighted six genes: Wee1, Rbl1, Gnl3, Mdm2, Cdk2 and Ccne2. Proteomic validation and human SPLiT-seq data supported their relevance, but these are correlative findings in mice.
ai_technology: Contrastive deep-learning framework with triplet loss, interpreted with SHAP
organization: University Health Network; Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute

evidence.tested: Proteomic validation in mouse models and comparison with human SPLiT-seq data.
evidence.unknown: Sample sizes are not given; causal roles of the genes are untested. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning mapped regenerative trajectories and ranked predictive genes.
